clue.text: Where one heard the rumour about wine-maker?

definitions.meaning: gossip passed on informally is said to be heard through this plant, in the idiom
the climbing plant that bears the fruit pressed for wine, so it makes wine

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for gossip spread by word of mouth names this climbing plant, which also bears the fruit winemaking needs.

clue.text: Sympathy could make one hit the bottle?

parts.note: to rap is to hit or knock sharply
port is a fortified wine, the bottle in the sense of drink

explanation.surface: Getting on well with someone might drive a person to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sympathetic bond or harmonious understanding between people is the relation named.

clue.text: Chat to new model

parts.note: patter is fast glib talk, chat

explanation.surface: Making conversation with a newly hired fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A model to be copied, like a dressmaker's template, is a synonym.

clue.text: First book of the series? No, it goes back to exercise of free will

parts.note: VOL is short for volume, one book of a series
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

indicators.note: goes back tells us the words no and it are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rejects the opening volume of a series and sends it back by choice.
explanation.walkthrough: VOL I is how the first volume of a series is labelled; 'goes back' turns NO IT into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising free will means choosing for oneself, which is what this word for a deliberate act of choosing describes.

clue.text: A way out, for example, returning on a ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the earlier pieces sit above the one that follows

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
re- is the prefix meaning back or again, as in coming back, so returning gives these letters
SS stands for steamship, a ship

explanation.surface: One escape route, say, is going back aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit or means of leaving is the Latin-derived word for a passage outwards.

clue.text: Buyers confronted by excise men in the queen's name

indicators.note: in places the royal cipher inside the officials' word here

parts.note: Customs officers are the officials who collect excise duties
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher that stands for the queen's name

explanation.surface: Shoppers are challenged by customs officers acting on royal authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who buy from a shop or business are its clientele, the people it serves.

clue.text: Hard to see the ring the scientist dropped over the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, dropped over means placed above the piece that comes next

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
BSc, Bachelor of Science, is a science graduate
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A ring vanishes from view after a researcher lets it fall into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the scientist' is not Curie or Newton but a science graduate, BSC. The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dim, concealed or indistinct is not easily made out.

clue.text: Spider set out and kept on going

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spider, once set loose, kept crawling along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of SPIDER SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on doggedly regardless of difficulty is to continue stubbornly.

clue.text: Complain about the last annoying noise

indicators.note: the last of annoying means only that word's final letter is taken

parts.note: a rumble is a deep rolling noise

explanation.surface: Moaning about the most recent irritating sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan or grouse is to voice discontent, the same as to gripe.

clue.text: Sprinkle salt up a kitchen utensil

indicators.note: to sprinkle is to scatter, so the letters of these three words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Shaking salt onto a cooking tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprinkle' looks like an instruction about seasoning, but it rearranges SALT UP A.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, broad-bladed tool for lifting, turning or spreading food is a common kitchen implement.

clue.text: Hospital department offers desserts, which is tempting

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
ices are frozen desserts

explanation.surface: A hospital ward offering ice creams is appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is tempting another person lures or allures them, so the verb fits the phrase.

clue.text: Government officials on leave meeting men of the trees?

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, staffed by government officials
people on leave are taking a rest, so they are resters

explanation.surface: Civil servants on holiday meet people who work in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who manage woodland, tending and protecting its timber, are woodsmen.

clue.text: City father with a habit of wolfing down his food?

definitions.text: City father with a habit of wolfing down his food?

parts.words: City father with a habit of wolfing down his food
parts.note: the legendary founder of a great city, who as a baby was suckled by a she-wolf, so his food came from a wolf

explanation.surface: A city councillor known for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend makes this twin the founder of Rome, nursed by a she-wolf alongside his brother Remus.

clue.text: A very large case for the evangelist to carry German coins

indicators.note: a case holds something, so the size letters surround the saint here
to carry means to hold inside, so the saint sits within the size letters

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning very large
St Mark, author of the second Gospel, is one of the four evangelists

explanation.surface: An enormous suitcase for the gospel writer to transport German money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' and 'to carry' put OS (outsize) around ST MARK.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the currency units of East Germany before reunification.

clue.text: Punch with venom, love!

parts.note: a sting delivers venom, and stands in for it here
O is love, a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Striking with a poisonous jab, darling!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' is not a blow or a drink here but vigour: the answer is an old word for strength or zest, and also a strong ale.
explanation.definitionFit: In old slang the word means vigour or force, the kick of strong drink.

clue.text: Grubby producers of luxury material

parts.note: grubby means being grubs, larvae, which spin the costly fibre rather than being dirty

explanation.definitionFit: These moth larvae spin cocoons whose fibre is woven into fine fabric.

clue.text: They received letters on a festive occasion, note, and gave a short reply

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
TI is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
ANS is the abbreviation of answer, a reply

explanation.surface: People got mail at a party, then a note, and sent a brief response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' are not post but epistles: St Paul wrote to the early church in a region of Asia Minor.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's epistle was addressed to the early Christians of a region in Asia Minor.

clue.text: Do away with road initially that's ring-shaped

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or abolish
a British main road is an A road, and its initials give the letter A followed by R

explanation.surface: Abolish the ring road first.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain main roads are labelled A roads (the A1, A40), so 'road initially' is read as the initials of A road.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like a ring or circle, from the Latin anulus, a little ring.

clue.text: Suitable that it may be due to fitness

parts.note: apt means suitable or fitting
taken as written

indicators.note: may be suggests the word due could be something else once its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A proper reason may be put down to physical fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges DUE into UDE, while IT is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural ability or suitability for a task is what fitness means here.

clue.text: Declare likely limits for a large home

parts.note: to declare is to state

indicators.note: the limits of likely are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Announce the likely boundaries of a big house.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the British phrase for a grand country mansion open to visitors, so the adjective is what a large home is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and imposing, the adjective classically paired with home for a British country mansion.

clue.text: Woodlouse, perhaps, messing up cop's id

indicators.note: messing up means jumbling, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woodlouse is spoiling a policeman's identity card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing up' rearranges COPSID. 'perhaps' warns that the answer is only loosely a woodlouse: it is a booklouse or barklouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny insect of the order Psocoptera, such as a booklouse or barklouse, loosely likened to a woodlouse.

clue.text: Applause that eggs on tenor a little bit

parts.note: ova are eggs
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music
an ion is a tiny charged particle, a little bit

explanation.surface: Clapping that encourages a singer just a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eggs on' reads as encourages, but 'eggs' gives OVA and 'on' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst of enthusiastic clapping, often standing, is an outpouring of acclaim.

clue.text: Sluggishness experienced, however I tear in

indicators.note: however means in whatever way, so the letters may be arranged in any order

explanation.surface: A sense of torpor is felt even though I rip into things.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency to stay inactive or resist change is lethargy.

clue.text: Mud a tank splashed around in Nepalese city

indicators.note: splashed around means scattered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tank churns through mud in a Himalayan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Nepal, in an older spelling without the H.

clue.text: Searched for an act to imprison 55

indicators.note: to imprison means to hold inside, so the act's letters surround the number

parts.note: a deed is an act
LV is 55 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Looked for a deed that would lock up 55.
explanation.walkthrough: '55' looks like a cross-reference, but it is the number in Roman numerals, LV.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig deep into records or a bag is to search thoroughly.

clue.text: Totted up points at which rug is knotted in

parts.note: E and S are points of the compass, east and south

indicators.note: in means the rug sits inside the word for knotted

parts.note: something knotted is tied
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: Counted the spots where a carpet gets knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totted up' sounds like exact sums, but an approximate reckoning fits; 'is ... in' signals the container, with 'at which' only linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Totting up is adding figures roughly, giving a reckoned or approximate total.

clue.text: Being heard by 12 or 27

parts.note: a court case being heard before a jury of twelve, or before legal experts as in 27 across

explanation.definitionFit: A defendant whose case is before a court is being tried.

clue.text: They're bound to find out about the crime

definitions.text: They're bound to find out about the crime

parts.words: They're bound to find out about the crime
parts.note: bound reads as tied up, but these legal experts are duty-bound to look into criminal matters

explanation.definitionFit: Experts in law, whose work is to examine crime and its legal treatment.

clue.text: I object to the way one's taken in this girl

parts.note: me is the object form of I

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the numeral sits within the way

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: I protest at the way this girl gets fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' is not a protest: ME is the grammatical object form of I.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so 'this girl' points to a forename.

clue.text: Lend a nice outfit every ten years

indicators.note: outfit as a verb means to fit out afresh, so the letters are refitted in a new order

explanation.surface: Lend someone a smart outfit once a decade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' looks like clothing but rearranges LEND A NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring once a decade, recurring at intervals of a decade.
